lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.note: Chapter title. Leave a clean beat before story begins.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: No one spoke after BAYL-ID-din's final words.

lines.speaker: Bel-iddin
lines.note: Text calls this 'Bel-iddin's final words' though Zik spoke it at the end of Ch.17. CHECK attribution.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The journal lay closed between them.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Rain dripped from the reed canopy into the basin beside the well. Somewhere beyond the courtyard wall a donkey brayed, followed by an argument over whether it belonged to the temple or to the man trying to drag it away.

lines.speaker: Balag
lines.text: If we're doing this again, we leave prepared.

lines.speaker: Ninsun
lines.text: I'll inventory what we already have.

lines.speaker: Enhedu
lines.text: I'll see what can be bought without attracting attention.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Zeek tightened the satchel across his shoulder.

lines.speaker: Zik
lines.text: My equipment is still at my mother's house.

lines.speaker: Zik
lines.text: You know me better than that.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: He stepped into the evening streets.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The streets were still crowded with evening traffic. Pilgrims moved toward the temples in loose, chanting groups. Merchants dragged carts through the torchlit haze. Prostitutes leaned in the shadows beneath painted doorways, calling to men who pretended not to hear them. Priests moved through the crowd with the self-important expressions of men who believed the gods had personally appointed them to supervise everyone else's mistakes.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Zeek preferred the city when it was loud. Noise gave a man cover. In a crowd, people saw what they expected to see: a trader, a scavenger, another hungry bastard trying to make enough silver to survive the month.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: His own tools remained at his mother's house.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: He headed toward his mother's, keeping to the shadows out of habit. Halfway there he noticed the first wrong thing.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: A temple scribe was watching him from across the street.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The man was young, well-dressed, and clean enough to look suspicious on principle. His linen robe was too fine for the neighborhood, and the wax tablet tucked beneath his arm was decorated with a small silver seal. He was the kind of man who usually never looked twice at men like Zeek.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Zeek slowed near a stall selling bronze chisels. The scribe stopped.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Zeek did not look back again. He changed direction twice, moving through the evening crowd with the casual rhythm of a man who had nowhere particular to be. He passed a spice seller, crossed behind a row of pottery stalls, and slipped into a narrow alley between a wine merchant's warehouse and a shuttered bakery.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The alley smelled of old water and rotting grain. Zeek waited.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The scribe entered thirty seconds later.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Zeek stepped out behind him and pressed a knife lightly against his side.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Zik
lines.text: That wasn't one of the options.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The young man swallowed. Zeek pressed the blade a little harder. Not enough to cut. Enough to remind him that the distinction was temporary.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: False Scribe
lines.text: He would like to speak with you again.

lines.speaker: Zik
lines.text: That sounded less like a request.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The scribe glanced toward the mouth of the alley. No one was there. The crowd moved past without looking in.

lines.speaker: False Scribe
lines.text: The Collector is prepared to offer ten times what you received today.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: False Scribe
lines.text: Or anything else you removed from the chamber.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: For a moment the alley seemed to contract around them. Zeek had never mentioned the journal. He had never told the Collector about the chamber beneath the desert. He had never told him about the skeleton. He had never told him about the symbol appearing beneath his skin.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The scribe knew about all of it. Or enough of it.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The scribe's mouth opened. Nothing came out.

lines.speaker: False Scribe
lines.text: He says the mark has a way of announcing itself.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Zeek looked down at his palm. The symbol was barely visible beneath the skin—a faint discoloration, an old scar if a man didn't know what he was looking at.

lines.speaker: False Scribe
lines.text: Especially to those who have seen it before.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The words settled between them. Zeek slowly removed the knife.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The scribe turned to face him.
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The scribe's face had gone pale.

lines.speaker: False Scribe
lines.text: The Collector says you should not go back.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The scribe said nothing. That was answer enough.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The scribe's eyes flicked toward the knife.

lines.speaker: Zik
lines.text: Did he tell you what happens if I do?

lines.speaker: Zik
lines.text: Then you have wasted both our time.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The scribe hurried past him, then stopped at the end of the alley.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Zeek looked over his shoulder. The scribe's face had changed. The nervousness was gone. For just a second he looked older.

lines.speaker: False Scribe
lines.text: Some doors are sealed because what is behind them is dangerous.
lines.note: Nervousness gone; suddenly older. Slower, calmer, lower.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The scribe's eyes dropped to the mark on Zeek's palm.

lines.speaker: False Scribe
lines.text: Some are sealed because the thing behind them is still waiting.
lines.note: Nervousness gone; suddenly older. Slower, calmer, lower.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The words should have sounded like a threat. Instead they sounded familiar. He hated that.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: When Zeek returned to his mother's house to gather the last of his gear, he found the second wrong thing.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The crack in the frame was exactly where he had left it. Nothing looked disturbed.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Zeek stood in the hallway for nearly a minute without entering.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: His father had taught him to notice things that were about to fail. He had also taught him that a room could tell you when someone had been inside it. A moved object. A displaced grain of dust. A door closed with the wrong amount of force.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The small clay tablet he used as a weight for papers was on the table. It had been beside the window.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: His spare knife was beneath his pallet. It had been on the shelf.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: His father's measuring cord still hung beside the doorway.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: BAYL-ID-din had always coiled it clockwise.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Someone had hung it back the other way.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: And the loose brick behind which he kept emergency coin was slightly askew.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Zeek closed the door behind him.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: He did not wake his mother.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: He crossed the room and crouched beside the wall. The brick had been replaced carefully. Too carefully. He pulled it free.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The emergency coins were still there. He counted them anyway.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: He put them back and examined the brick. A small smear of pale dust marked one edge. Someone had removed it. Someone had put it back. Someone had been careful enough to leave the money untouched.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Zeek sat on the edge of his pallet for a long moment.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: His mother breathed softly in her sleep. The kiln beneath the house gave a low, constant rumble. The room was warm. Familiar. Safe.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Zeek looked at the journal in his hands.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The mark on his palm throbbed in time with his heartbeat. He had lied to the Collector. But the Collector had already known he was lying. That was the part Zeek couldn't fit into the arithmetic.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: A lie was a transaction. You gave someone a falsehood and received something in return: information, time, distance, safety.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: But the Collector had not been negotiating with him. He had been waiting.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Zeek opened the journal. The pages were blank. He turned to the map.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The vertical section was still there. The rivers. The impossible structures. The spiral descending through the layers of the world.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: At the bottom of the map, beneath the words I WAS WRONG ABOUT THE DEPTH, there was now a second line.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: He had not seen it before.

lines.speaker: Bel-iddin
lines.text: I WAS WRONG ABOUT WHO WAS LOOKING.
lines.note: New line in Bel-iddin's hand, still wet.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Not because he doubted the words.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Because he was trying to remember whether they had existed a heartbeat earlier.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: He looked toward the sleeping pallet. His mother had not moved.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The house was silent except for the kiln. He looked back at the journal.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The ink beneath the sentence was still wet.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The mark in his palm burned. He pulled his hand away.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The leather settled beneath his hand.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The kiln rumbled beneath the floor exactly as it had every night since he was a child.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Nothing inside the room had changed.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Zeek slung the satchel over his shoulder.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Instead he repaired the cracked frame with two careful pushes of his thumb until the wood sat flush again.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Then he stepped into the alley.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Halfway to the street the journal moved.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The mark beneath the linen pulsed once.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Then, from somewhere deep beneath Uruk, something answered.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Zeek stood motionless in the alley.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: He looked toward the dark western quarter where the others would be waiting before dawn.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Then back toward his mother's house.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: It felt as though it had received an answer.
